**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via inlineHelpText (literal, a string literal in translateObject))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`  _(via inlineHelpText (literal, a string literal in translateObject))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via inlineHelpText (literal, a string literal in translateObject))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via inlineHelpText (literal, a string literal in translateObject))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via inlineHelpText (literal, a string literal in translateObject))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 14208f2c504ff6f1529be8a28323a91df53d0562` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `def6773c5068eb0ac7d85759353e630efb76b4d8` — the merge of head `e1451dc02f544a7024084fc622ac218a6ba8407a` into base `14208f2c504ff6f1529be8a28323a91df53d0562`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin def6773c5068eb0ac7d85759353e630efb76b4d8 && git checkout def6773c5068eb0ac7d85759353e630efb76b4d8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 14208f2c504ff6f1529be8a28323a91df53d0562 e1451dc02f544a7024084fc622ac218a6ba8407a && git checkout -B drift-repro 14208f2c504ff6f1529be8a28323a91df53d0562 && git merge --no-ff e1451dc02f544a7024084fc622ac218a6ba8407a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 14208f2c504ff6f1529be8a28323a91df53d0562
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 14208f2c504ff6f1529be8a28323a91df53d0562` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts`** — judged against the seat's ruling on #29153 (translated help is served on the slot the console reads first, one derivation across extractor, resolver and console, no new key), ADR-0029 D9.2a (comparison-based provenance, one predicate), and its first consumers: the `GET /api/v1/meta/object/:name` read (meta-item-read-gate.ts) and the public form (form-routes.ts), rendered by the console's `fieldHelpText`.

Attempts to break it, each read in the live tree at the head:

1. *Tenant edits `inlineHelpText` only.* Served value ≠ packaged → diverged → kept; `description` (undiverged) still receives the translation; the console draws the tenant's text. Holds (pinned through `translateMetadataDocument` in both locales).
2. *Field the packaged base does not declare (extension field).* `packagedObjectField` returns `{}` (L1966), `{}.inlineHelpText !== value` → diverged → authored text kept. Holds, pinned.
3. *No packaged base* (runtime object, or `getPackagedObjectBase` undefined). Predicate answers false → catalog applies. Holds, pinned.
4. *Idempotence / double translation.* After one pass the served `inlineHelpText` differs from the packaged → the second pass keeps it. Holds (the same property D9.2a records for scalars).
5. *Studio round-trip pollution.* Studio's designer loads `/meta/:type/:name/layers` (ResourceEditPage.tsx L7), a STORED-version door the rest gate does not translate; only the plain read goes through `translateMetaItem`. So a zh-CN Studio save does not freeze the translation into the overlay. The ADR's recorded "honest edge" (a client that PUTs the plain read back) applies to `inlineHelpText` exactly as it already does to `description` and `label`; nothing new.
6. *Fallback chain.* zh-CN lacking `help` while `en` carries it serves the `en` entry onto `inlineHelpText`; with extractor-written bundles that is the authored text, and a hand-edited `en` entry wins over the authored text exactly as it already does for `label` and `description` (`catalog ?? document`). Consistent, not new.
7. *`fieldPatches` (ADR-0146 D10).* An extension that patches a vendor field's `inlineHelpText` makes the served value diverge from the owner-alone base (`getPackagedObjectBase`, protocol.ts L9437: scalars are the owner's), so the catalog yields and that patched text is served untranslated in every locale. This is the same consequence `description` already has under the same rule and is what the ruling asked for ("same per-slot divergence rule"); recorded, no fix owed in this PR.
8. *The docblock's citations.* Extractor source and path (L1489), the console reader's name and package, and the `help` alias refusal in `FieldSchema` all match the live tree. The stale "which the extractor never reads" is gone.
9. *The accepted scenario (card reproduction).* `showcase_contact.lead_score` authors `inlineHelpText` only (contact.object.ts L67); the zh-CN bundle carries `help: 由评分规则计算,不可手动编辑。` (translations/index.ts L644); the packaged base is the showcase's code-owned object, so the served `inlineHelpText` equals it → translated → `fieldHelpText` draws the zh text. The new test restates exactly this fixture and the console read. i18n.surface-matrix negative[1] ("a surface whose group the spec declares showing NO translation while the bundle carries one is a FAIL against the resolver") is answered at the resolver.

Findings:

- **should-fix (S1)** — `ObjectFieldLike` (L3604-3612) declares `inlineTitle?: string` because the translator writes it, but not `inlineHelpText`, which the translator now writes too; the slot is reached only through the `[key: string]: any` index signature and re-typed by a `typeof` guard. Declare `inlineHelpText?: string` beside `inlineTitle` (optional member, additive, still patch).
- **should-fix (S2)** — test "CONTROL: the source locale serves the authored `inlineHelpText` untouched" cannot fail on what it names: the fixture's `en` bundle entry equals the authored text, and the resolver writes the requested locale's own entry on the source locale too (`localeChain` skips only the fallbacks). The slot is rewritten with an identical string, so the assertion pins nothing the first test does not. Either state what it pins (the extractor-mirrored `en` entry round-trips) or make the control real: drop the `en` `help` entry and assert the authored text survives.
- No must-fix. The change holds against the extractor, the console reader, the served doors and ADR-0029 D9.2a, and it answers the card's reproduction.
